title: Evening oncall: probabilistic link-reset heuristics and handoff notes
content:
Context / motivation:
This is a working sketch for the evening/night oncall team that documents a lightweight, probabilistic approach to handling intermittent GPU interconnect link resets (observed as transient NVLink negotiation failures, correctable ECC bursts followed by driver restarts, or sporadic kernel panics on the inference fleet).

Why this doc exists (symptoms we keep seeing):
- nodes report short-lived 'link down' / 'link training failed' events in dmesg for a single NVLink port, usually followed by corrective driver unload/load or a GPU process crash within 30–120s.
- ECC correctable-error counters spike for 1–5 minutes then return to baseline. No persistent memory corruption observed most of the time.
- In ~10% of these clusters, the GPU driver hits a fatal and the node goes into a KMS hang requiring reboot.
- Incidents are bursty and difficult to reproduce in lab; they correlate weakly with thermal excursions and more strongly with firmware rollouts and recent PCIe BIOS updates.

High-level goal for oncall:
- Keep serving running with minimal disruption to latency SLOs. Prefer soft-eviction of noisy GPUs -> fallback routing -> limited node reboot only when necessary. Capture traces and telemetry for postmortem.

Evening/night quick triage checklist (first 10–20 minutes):
1) Identify scope
   - Check the alert: which cluster/pool/instance IDs?
   - Query console for error rates last 30m (tokens/req failures) and per-model latency spikes.
2) Confirm node health
   - ssh to node(s) if reachable. Run: `journalctl -b -u nvidia-driver.service -n 500 | grep -Ei "link|nvlink|ecc|gpu"` (collect output to /tmp/oncall-logs-<time>.log).
   - `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERF,LINK` to snapshot ECC counters and link state.
3) Short mitigation (non-disruptive first)
   - If ECC correctable error count is rising but processes still responsive: mark node as `drain:soft` in scheduler to stop new loads and allow in-flight to finish.
   - Increase request routing weight to healthy nodes (console quick route).
4) If driver PID crashed or GPU process hung
   - Try `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service` (soft) and watch for immediate recurrence for 5 minutes. If it restarts cleanly and counters remain stable -> leave drained for 10–30m and monitor.
5) If KMS hang or kernel panic occurred
   - Capture crash log (kmsg/serial) and schedule an urgent node reboot. Mark node Out-of-Service. Collect serial console output and attach to ticket.

Probabilistic heuristics for deciding escalate vs experiment locally (what worked empirically):
- If the same physical link/port shows repeated retraining events on >2 different GPUs within 24 hours, escalate to hardware/firmware team immediately (SRE-5392 tag).
- If driver restarts clear the condition and ECC counts fall, prefer automated soft-reclassify for 30–60 minutes (avoid immediate fleet reboots).
- If thermal delta >12C in preceding 15m around the PCIe connector area (sensor names start with pcie-*) consider retrieving recent airflow/slot history and open cooling ticket.

Telemetry queries and quick dashboards to check (copy these into the incident ticket):
- Aggregated `nvlink_retrain_count` per node, 1h/24h windows.
- `gpu_driver_restart_count` per kernel-version, grouped by firmware_version.
- ECC correctable vs uncorrectable counters per GPU over last 2h.
- Packet: `sum by(node) (increase(nvlink_events_total{type="training_fail"}[1h]))` (console query example).

Commands (do these in a controlled shell session and paste outputs into the ticket):
- `sudo dmesg --ctime | egrep -i "nvlink|link training|ecc|nvrm" | tail -n 200`
- `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,firmware,utilization.gpu,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv`
- `sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia` (only if instructed by SRE lead; may drop running containers).

Local experiments (quick and reversible):
- Toggle link retrain backoff: set `nvlink_retrain_backoff_ms` to a higher value for 10–30 minutes to avoid repeated negotiation thrash. This is a runtime knob exposed on some driver builds (only attempt with a teammate). Record exact value and timestamp.
- Temporarily lower scheduling pressure: reduce concurrent contexts on the suspect GPU by setting `max_concurrent_inference` for the node to 1–2. Observe for 15–20m.

Handoff notes for night -> morning team (what we must leave behind):
- Attach collected logs to the Jira ticket (SRE-5392). Filename: oncall-logs-<node>-<ts>.log.
- Note whether we ran a driver restart, modprobe cycle, kernel reboot. Timestamp each action and include stdout.
- If node rebooted, include serial console snapshot and the last `journalctl -k` lines.
- Tag firmware versions: driver_version, bios_version, gpu_firmware. Add them to ticket fields.
- Label the node `drain:soft` or `do-not-schedule` depending on whether we want automated reprovisioning.

Post-incident capture checklist (for follow-up and lab reproduction):
- Exact steps to reproduce (if any); start/end times; workload running (which model/sequence lengths).
- Correlate with recent infra changes: cloud BIOS/PCIe firmware rollouts, kernel updates, driver releases, or host kernel command line changes.
- Attach a minimal runbook attempt: reproduce with the same model, same concurrency, and synthetic ECC injection if feasible.

Suggested runbook additions (near-term):
1) Add an alert that fires when `nvlink_retrain_count > 5` for the same port in 30m AND `driver_restart_count >= 1` in 30m. Include runbook link and auto-create Jira SRE ticket.
2) Add a low-disruption automated response: after 2 retrains in 10 min, automatically soft-drain node and reduce routing weight. Leave human in loop for driver restart.
3) Add telemetry tags to capture PCIe slot and chassis rails to help correlate with hardware group.

Open hypotheses (to validate in lab):
- Hypothesis A: New NVLink firmware has a race condition with quick retrains under high small-request tail workloads, causing driver asserting in the link training state machine.
- Hypothesis B: A pattern of power noise on the GPU rail during bursty workloads is increasing ECC counts and causing the driver to trigger a recovery path.

Immediate next steps (owner + ETA):
- Maya Chen: attach logs and create SRE-5392 update, ETA 2029-05-15 11:00 PT.
- Diego: schedule a 2-hr lab window to try the backoff knob and reproduce with synthetic traffic, ETA 2029-05-17.
- Priya: add the alert conditions to the monitoring playbook and a simple auto-drain action, ETA 2029-05-20.

Notes to oncall: this is intentionally pragmatic and noisy — we prefer quick isolation and preserving serving over immediate fleet-wide reboots. If you are unsure, escalate to the SRE lead on call (pager code in the console) before touching modprobe/reboot on a production node.

Attachments (in ticket):
- /tmp/oncall-logs-<node>-<ts>.log (dmesg + nvidia-smi snapshots)
- serial-console-<node>-<ts>.txt
- dashboard-screenshot-nvlink-training-<cluster>.png

Triage snippets (examples pasted to ticket):
- "2029-05-12T20:18:34Z node-gpu-45: nvlink: link training failed on port 3 - retrying"
- "2029-05-12T20:19:05Z node-gpu-45: nvidia-driver[1243]: UVM unload triggered by process 20122"
- "2029-05-12T20:19:47Z node-gpu-45: ECC corrected errors incremented 82 -> 267 in 4m"

If nothing else, leave a one-line summary in the ticket: what you changed and why in plain english. That helps morning shift pick up cleanly.

End of sketch — please iterate. This doc will be expanded into the formal runbook once we validate backoff knob behavior in lab and agree on non-disruptive auto-drain thresholds.
